learning: Lookahead is monotone from y 0.04 to y 0.08 (131.9, 454.6, 534.0, 561.6). The next lever is track width, and the physical direction is now set by the contract's turn-rate equation: a narrower track gives more yaw per PWM count. The earlier wheel_track 0.14 suggestion was physically backwards and is withdrawn.
notes: Iteration 6 package: the Builder's wheel_track 0.10 geometry on the iteration 5 sensor layout (y 0.08), with the iteration 5 controller unchanged. The race isolates the track width, which sets yaw gain per unit of steering command.
rationale: Iteration 5 (y 0.08, wheel_track 0.12, score 561.6) is the best design so far. The lookahead sweep is monotone: y 0.04 gave 131.9, y 0.06 gave 454.6, y 0.07 gave 534.0, and y 0.08 gave 561.6. Oscillation stayed low (oval 0.20, s-bend 0.32), the oval finished 20 of 20, and the controller raised no errors. The s-bend is still the main loss, with 9 of 20 off-track exits and the highest control_effort of any track (12.2). Slalom is 0 of 20 with line_loss 1.35, which lookahead alone is unlikely to fix. The Builder's intent is to change only wheel_track, from 0.12 to 0.10. The contract defines turn rate as the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, and the PWM difference is set by turn times 350. A narrower track therefore gives about 20 percent more yaw per unit of steering command. I am keeping the controller identical to iteration 5 (kp 4.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [2,1,0,-1,-2]). This keeps the race a clean one-variable test, and control_effort stays comparable because it scales with kp. Risk: the extra yaw gain may raise steering_oscillation, so if it rises above about 0.4 or the oval finish falls below 0.85, the next step is either wheel_track 0.12 (the best known design) or a lower kp at the narrower track. I expect the s-bend off-track count and control_effort to fall, with the oval holding near 1.0.
